title: Nell and the Cold Night
series: Nell and the Night Garden — Reading Adventures
readingLevel: UK Year 2–3. Short sentences, mostly high-frequency words, a few sparkle words (greenhouse, lantern, jackdaws).

greenhouse.prompt: Felix is cold. What does he need? Pick three.
greenhouse.wrongFeedback: Nell thought again. What did Grandma Fen say?

p1.text: Nell woke up in the middle of the night. Something was wrong. The garden was dark. It was never dark. Every night, the greenhouse glowed blue at the bottom of the garden. That was Felix. Tonight, the glow was gone. Nell jumped out of bed and pulled on her boots.

p2.text: Nell ran to Grandma Fen's room. "Grandma! Felix has stopped glowing!" Grandma Fen sat up fast. "Then he is cold," she said. "A Luminis Radix must never get cold. Listen to me, Nell. This is important."

p3.text: "Felix needs three things when he is cold," said Grandma Fen. "A lantern. A blanket. And a song. Not a torch. A lantern. Torches are too bright for him." Nell nodded. Lantern. Blanket. Song.

p4.text: "One more thing," said Grandma Fen. "Go past the pond. Never go past the shed at night. That is where the jackdaws sleep, and they wake up very cross." "Pond, not shed," said Nell. "Go," said Grandma Fen.

p5.text: Nell ran to the kitchen. On the table was a torch. On the hook was a key. Nell looked. Then she saw it, by the door. The old yellow lantern. She picked it up. It was heavy and warm. "One," said Nell.

p6.text: Next, the hall. Nell pulled the wool blanket off the big chair. It was soft and red. She held it tight. "Two," said Nell.

p7.text: The last thing was not in a room. It was in Nell's head. Grandma Fen sang it every night in the greenhouse. A little humming song. Nell hummed it now, very quietly, so she would not forget. "Three," said Nell.

p8.text: Nell opened the back door. The garden was black. Cold air bit her nose. The path went two ways. Left, past the pond. Right, past the shed. Nell stopped. Which way had Grandma Fen said?

p9a.text: Nell went right, past the shed. Big mistake. The jackdaws woke up. CAW! CAW! CAW! Black wings flapped in her face. Nell ran back to the door as fast as she could. Her heart went thump, thump, thump. "Not the shed," she said. "The pond."

p9b.text: Nell went left, past the pond. The water was still and quiet. A frog plopped. That was all. She could see the greenhouse now. It was dark. Nell had never seen it dark before. She walked faster.

p10.text: Nell opened the greenhouse door. Inside, Felix was small and grey. His leaves hung down. He did not glow at all. "Felix," Nell whispered. "I'm here." She put her bag down. "Now. What do you need?"

p11.text: Nell lit the lantern. Soft yellow light filled the greenhouse. She tucked the blanket around Felix's pot. Then she hummed the little song. Slowly, slowly, a tiny blue light came on in his leaves. Then another. Then another. Felix glowed. "There you are," said Nell.

p12.text: Behind her, the door opened. Grandma Fen stood there in her big coat, with two mugs of hot chocolate. "Well done," she said. "I knew you would remember." And they sat in the blue light together, until the sun came up.

media.stylePrefix: Children's picture-book illustration, painterly gouache texture, soft edges, deep navy night palette with warm amber accents, gentle rim light, cosy English garden at night, storybook, no text, no watermark.  ## Motion suffix (append to every image-to-video prompt — Kling has no negative-prompt box, so the negatives live here)  Very subtle ambient motion only. Slow, gentle, looping. The camera is completely static: no zoom, no pan, no drift. No people, no faces, no hands. No text or watermark. Nothing new appears, nothing changes shape, no morphing, no flicker. Everything else in the picture stays exactly as it is.  ## Scenes  | scene id | still prompt | motion prompt | |---|---|---| | `bedroom-dark` | A child's bedroom at night seen from the pillow, window with curtains half open, beyond the window a dark garden and at the very bottom a small dark greenhouse with no light in it. Nothing else moves. | | `grandma-room` | An old woman's bedroom at night, a big wooden bed with a patchwork quilt, a bedside lamp just switched on casting warm amber light, books stacked everywhere, a cat asleep at the foot of the bed. No people. | Lamp glow pulses very slightly as if just warming up. Cat's side rises and falls. | | `kitchen-night` | A cottage kitchen at night lit by a single bulb, wooden table with a small torch on it, a key hanging on a hook by the window, and an old brass-and-glass lantern by the back door, glass slightly fogged. | The bare bulb sways almost imperceptibly on its cord, its light shifting very slightly on the table. Nothing else moves. No fog, no smoke, no steam. | | `hall-night` | A narrow cottage hallway at night, a big armchair with a red wool blanket thrown over it, a pair of small wellington boots by the front door, coats on pegs, faint light from the kitchen behind. | Coat hem sways as if a draught passed. Light from the kitchen flickers softly. | | `garden-fork` | View from a back doorstep at night: directly ahead a gravel garden path forks into two clearly separate paths in the foreground, like a letter Y. The left fork curves away toward a moonlit pond. The right fork leads toward a dark wooden shed with no lights, black windows. Cold mist. Stars. | Grass sways. Mist drifts low across both paths. Stars twinkle. | | `shed-jackdaws` | A dark wooden garden shed at night, completely unlit, black windows, five jackdaws on the roof with wings half-spread and eyes catching the moonlight, feathers scattered in the air. Dramatic but not scary. | Feathers drift down. Wings twitch. One jackdaw's eye blinks. | | `pond-night` | A small garden pond at night, perfectly still water reflecting a full moon, reeds at the edge, a frog on a lily pad, in the far distance a greenhouse with no light. | The frog stays perfectly still on its lily pad and does not move at all. Only the water moves: a single slow ripple spreads outward across the moon's reflection. Reeds sway very gently. | | `greenhouse-dark` | Inside a Victorian glass greenhouse at night, all shadows and moonlit panes, and in the centre on a wooden bench a single small plant in a clay pot with its leaves drooping, grey and dull. Sad and quiet. | Moonlight through the glass slowly brightens and dims as thin cloud passes. A few tiny specks of dust glint in the light. Nothing else moves. No smoke, no mist, no wisps. | | `greenhouse-glow` | The same greenhouse interior, now lit by a warm brass lantern on the bench and, at the centre, a small plant whose leaves glow soft electric blue from within, light spilling across the glass panes, a red blanket tucked around the pot. Wonder. | Blue glow breathes gently, brightening and dimming on a slow cycle. Lantern flame flickers. Tiny motes of blue light rise from the leaves. |  The two greenhouse scenes are the emotional payoff. Spend most of your credits there. Generate `greenhouse-dark` first, then make `greenhouse-glow` from the same still with an edit pass so the room is identical and only the light changes — that continuity is what makes the ending land.  ## Making it loop  Models don't reliably produce seamless loops. Take the 8s clip and cross-fade its tail into its head:  ```bash ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -filter_complex \ "[0:v]split[a][b];[a]trim=0:7,setpts=PTS-STARTPTS[a1];[b]trim=7:8,setpts=PTS-STARTPTS[b1];[a1][b1]xfade=transition=fade:duration=1:offset=6[v]" \ -map "[v]" -an -c:v libx264 -pix_fmt yuv420p -movflags +faststart -crf 26 loop.mp4 ```  Then `-vf "scale=1280:-2"` if the file is over ~3MB. Muted, `playsinline`, `loop`, `autoplay` on the `<video>` tag.  ## What to do if the video looks bad  Use the still with a slow CSS pan (`transform: scale(1.08)` over 20s, ease, alternate). It is 90% as good and costs nothing. Don't let the media block the test — the thesis is the reading, not the pictures.
